findings.text: the skip returns on every repeated reading, so a lane whose counter stops advancing while requests are running no longer backs the width off at all. Measured on one controlled surface (10 streams, running=10, waiting=4, prefix hit 0.99, kv 0.28, counter then frozen): at the base revision the width walks 14->12->10->8->6->4, one down-step per 16-scrape window, each on 'stepping down: 0.0 tokens/s per stream is below the 10 floor', while at this revision it holds 14 with zero down-steps (sideeffects-base.log, sideeffects-head.log). A repeated reading and a livelocked engine are therefore indistinguishable to the controller, which is the one behaviour the docstring at imas_ambix/agent/router.py:621-623 still claims separately ('a per-stream rate of zero is what a stalled lane looks like'). The two are separable by the duration of the repeat streak -- an advance interval is tens of seconds while a stall lasts longer -- and no state tracks it; a sentence in the evidence or a bounded streak would name the trade.

the early return sits before both the throughput windows and the health sample, so while the counter repeats every judgement not derived from the counter samples at half rate. On a lane whose counter advances on every other scrape, a sustained prefix-hit collapse (0.90 against the 0.95 floor) steps the width at scrape 14 at the base revision and scrape 29 here -- 7.0 against 14.5 minutes at the 30 s cadence -- and the genuinely slow lane of the new test moves the same way (its step-down lands at scrape 15 at the base and 30 here). This is inherent to skipping the reading whole; a repeated reading could instead contribute a health sample with rate=None, which _controller_guard already tolerates (None entries are filtered per column at imas_ambix/agent/router.py:853, 866, 875) -- keeping the prefix and KV guards sampling every scrape while never letting a repeat score as a stall. If the added latency is intended, it belongs in the evidence text beside the repair.

the section points a reader at these samples as the live defect window, but the recorder stores one reading per minute while the controller differences consecutive 30 s scrapes: at the recorded cadence no consecutive pair repeats, so a literal replay steps the width at neither revision (0 down-steps at the base, no positive control), while holding each recorded reading across its minute's two scrapes reproduces the base failure at the live cadence (14->12->10->8, three down-steps 8 min apart, against lane.json's recorded 14->12->10 at 09:34/09:42/09:50) and holds 14 at this revision. A sentence here would save the next reader the reconstruction; the replay logs sit beside this review under ~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20260926T115931246263-review-of-s14-controller-ignores-repeated-readings/.
